subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, warn visibly and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: This controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and OpenClaw policy treats auth/provider routing and fallback behavior as security- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Require proof and fail-closed or visible warning
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main spawn proves OAuth inheritance and maintainers choose fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split fallback visibility after OAuth proof
options.body: Close only after live proof confirms OAuth inheritance, then track user-visible fallback warning or fail-closed policy in a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Accept current log-only fallback
options.body: Maintain the current logged fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require proof and fail-closed or visible warning
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main spawn proves OAuth inheritance and maintainers choose fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from current blame and recent work across auth-profile store ownership, Codex bridge behavior, subagent seams, and fallback logging.
